# The catalog spec's count table lists one group per line

## Context

On 19 Nov, examples PRs on *different* groups conflicted on one line of the catalog spec's count table. #21492 changed the Apps row (`[6, 4]` → `[6, 5]`); #21464 had changed the Lists row (`[12, 0]`) and #21491 the Charts row (`[5, 1]`) on the same physical line. Each needed a re-merge, a fresh CI run and, because the Fleet counts only approvals on the current head, a fresh approval. #21464 had been green and approved ten minutes earlier.

#21484 made this table the one literal per group. Its first AC reads "A new covered example changes one line in the unit spec (its family's row)", but the table packs four or five rows per line, so a row's line is shared with up to four other groups.

## The Problem

The examples lanes under #21140 and #21367 are per group: Lists, Charts, Forms, More components and so on. Two PRs from different lanes change different rows, which git can merge on its own unless the rows share a line or sit on adjacent lines. Measured on `dev` at `ed4435cf68`, by bumping each group's row in a throwaway commit and merging every pair: 98 of the 210 cross-group pairs conflict (46.7%). #21518 and #21519 add more catalog PRs before the 22 Nov lock.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/view/examples/MainContainerController.spec.mjs`, `groupCounts` (lines 703–709 on `dev` at `ed4435cf68`): 21 groups as `[home count, count from other groups]` on five lines, `recordCount` beside it. `publishedCount`, `groupCount` and `uncoveredCount` derive from them (#21486).
- Key order matters: line 229 maps `Object.values(groupCounts)` onto the mobile index's counts in route order, so the table keeps definition order.
- `buildScripts/util/check-block-alignment.mjs` (pre-commit, `--fix --staged`) aligns a block's colons, so the keys pad to the longest, `'multi-window'` (Ada, on the fork).
- git's merge conflicts on changes to adjacent lines as well as on the same line.
- Design authority: n/a. This changes test layout and calls no product behaviour wrong.

## The Fix

`groupCounts` lists one group per line, in definition order, keys padded to `'multi-window'`. No value changes and no other line moves. The same measurement on that layout leaves 20 of 210 pairs conflicting (9.5%): exactly the 20 pairs of neighbouring groups.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `groupCounts` holds one group per line, in definition order, and the catalog unit spec passes with no other change.
- [ ] AC-2: The PR carries the pairwise merge receipt for both layouts: on the new one only neighbouring groups conflict.
- [ ] AC-3: `check-block-alignment` passes on the table.

## Out of Scope

- `recordCount` stays one literal (#21484's choice), so two PRs that both add a record still collide there.
- `ExamplesCatalogNL.spec.mjs`, the catalog data and the Portal views.

## Avoided Traps

- **Same-group additions.** With one row per line, two PRs that add to the *same* group make the identical edit, and git merges it silently to a stale value: the trap #21484 named. It already exists for `recordCount`, and the catalog unit spec catches it on the merged head.
- **A blank line between rows.** It would clear the 20 neighbouring pairs too, at the cost of a 41-line table. Not worth it while lanes rarely own two neighbouring groups at once.
- **No literals at all.** #21484 kept one literal per group on purpose: it is the one place a spec says which group gained what.
